description: Shortlist neighbourhoods in England (London in depth) for a household: budget, bedrooms, weighted priorities (crime, station access, price level, official deprivation decile, noise, disorder, energy rating, leasehold share) and optional stations or local authorities to live near (regions narrows to English regions, e.g. ['london']; with no regions, stations or boroughs all of England is searched). Returns ranked areas: present them by rank, never by score (scores often tie; rankBasis says what orders them), with standing 0-100, meets ('4 of 5') and aheadBecause to explain the order; factor values, typicalPrice (the median recent sale), estimatedPrice and budgetFit (with property_type the type's own figure, priceBasis says which; else a ballpark for the bedroom count), postcode districts and website links. A deal-breaker needs must true (a range or place without it only ranks); mustStatus unknown (verified false) marks a must judged on a rail or straight-line estimate: those areas rank after the verified ones, so check that journey on the web. A ranked criterion an area has no data for (no crime is published for Greater Manchester) counts as half a fit and is named in that area's notScored: say so. Pass rejected areas in exclude_area_ids when refining after the user's feedback (LSOA, MSOA or local authority ids). The first tool for 'where should we live?'; rank_areas_by_metric sorts by one metric only, match_areas scores a ready preference-profile.v2, search_areas only turns names into ids.

label.description: What the point is, e.g. 'Crystal Palace NSC'.
label.title: Label

direction.description: higher = more of it (more A for balance/share, closer for nearest); lower = less. Default: the preset's.
direction.title: Direction

preset_id.description: A ready-made criterion from list_custom_presets, e.g. 'kebab-cafe'.
preset_id.title: Preset Id

formula.description: Prefer nearest for 'is one close' (straight-line walk minutes from the area's centre to the nearest A, up to 5 km) and per_resident for 'how much is around' (places in any set per 1,000 residents; the City of London is left out). The rest are counted inside each neighbourhood's boundary (the area shape on the map, not walking distance): count / density (per km² of the area) of places in any set; share A/(A+B); variety = distinct cuisines/sports among A; balance (A-B)/(A+B+5) from -1 (more B) to +1 (more A), advanced: few places keep an area near 0.
formula.title: Formula

label.description: Name the user will see: descriptive, no brand or value words, e.g. 'Kebab shops vs cafés'.
label.title: Label

radiusMetres.description: Kept for compatibility with saved criteria and share links (200-2000 m); no formula uses it, so leave the default.
radiusMetres.title: Radiusmetres

sets.description: Sets of places: a (required), b for balance/share, c optional for count/density.
sets.title: Sets

any.description: OR of matchers; a matcher ANDs OpenStreetMap tag tests over amenity, shop, leisure, tourism, sport, cuisine, healthcare, craft, office and brand: a value, a list of values, '*' (has the tag) or null (has no such tag). E.g. [{"cuisine": "kebab"}], [{"amenity": "cafe", "brand": null}] for independent cafés, [{"cuisine": "specialty_coffee"}] for coffee-led shops (specialty coffee, not a café with coffee on the menu; never a big chain), [{"brand": "Greggs"}]. religion/denomination are refused: places, not people.
any.title: Any

label.description: What the places are, e.g. 'Kebab shops'.
label.title: Label

any_of.description: Near either of 2-3 pinned points ('either pool', 'either office'): each area counts the quickest one.
any_of.title: Any Of

brand.description: With a category: only this brand, e.g. 'M&S', 'Waitrose', 'Lidl' (supermarket) or 'PureGym' (gym).
brand.title: Brand

category.description: Instead of a point: the nearest place of this kind (pool = public pool; step_free_station = a station TfL lists with lift access, or any DLR station or tram stop).
category.title: Category

center.description: Instead of latitude/longitude: [longitude, latitude], the `center` search_places returns.
center.title: Center

label.description: What the place is, e.g. 'Office', 'PureGym Angel', 'Any park'.
label.title: Label

latitude.description: A pinned place: its latitude (from search_places). For an address, `center` is its area's centre unless `centerPrecision` is `uprn`; never pin an LSOA centroid as the home.
latitude.title: Latitude

mode.description: How they get there (default transit for a pin, walk for a kind). car = typical weekday-morning traffic, no parking or charges: say so.
mode.title: Mode

must.description: True when an area beyond max_minutes is out of the question.
must.title: Must

school.description: Instead of top_school: the nearest school matching a filter (phase, Ofsted, type, intake, faith, one results measure ≥ a threshold), optionally within N metres; max_minutes still sets the trip.

school_rank_by.description: With top_school: rank by published results (default) or by Progress 8 (secondary only: progress pupils make from their primary results, latest published year 2023/24).
school_rank_by.title: School Rank By

top_school.description: Instead of a point or category: near one of London's top N state schools (by published results), e.g. 10. Living nearby never guarantees a place: say so.
top_school.title: Top School

direction.description: Which end the household prefers. Default: lower crime, shorter walks, lower prices, a higher deprivation decile, less noise, less disorder, more homes rated A-C, fewer leasehold sales.
direction.title: Direction

factor.description: crime = recorded crime rate; station-access = walk minutes to the nearest station; market-level = local £/m² price level; deprivation = official deprivation decile (IMD), 1 = most deprived; noise = share of homes at 55 dB+ from road, rail or aircraft; disorder = anti-social behaviour, criminal damage and public order per 1,000 residents; epc-share = share of homes rated EPC A-C (energy efficiency, running costs); leasehold-share = share of recent sales that were leasehold.
factor.title: Factor

must.description: True = a filter: only areas in the better half of London for it (no weight). False = ranked by importance: the better half fits fully, the next quarter of London partly, the rest not at all.
must.title: Must

importance.description: 1 nice to have … 5 essential: sets its place in the order.
importance.title: Importance

layer.description: Any map layer from list_metrics (e.g. noise, crime, station-access, nature-score, price-per-square-metre, food-hygiene), or disorder, epc-share, leasehold-share. Never a Census (census-*, student-share) layer. For schools use places=[{top_school: N}] or places=[{school: {...}}].
layer.title: Layer

must.description: True = a filter (no soft edge, no weight): a deal-breaker needs must true, else the range only ranks.
must.title: Must

scale.description: percentile = bounds are percentiles of the value within each area's region (London's areas among London's), 0 = lowest, 100 = highest (e.g. max 30 = the lowest 30% for noise); value = the layer's own unit.
scale.title: Scale

soft_max.description: Above max the fit falls to 0 at soft_max (≥ max).
soft_max.title: Soft Max

soft_min.description: Below min the fit falls to 0 at soft_min (≤ min).
soft_min.title: Soft Min

bad.description: What was wrong, missing or confusing.
bad.title: Bad

call_id.description: The callId of the answer you are rating.
call_id.title: Call Id

fix.description: The change to the tool or its answer you would want.
fix.title: Fix

good.description: What was useful in the answer.
good.title: Good

rating.description: 1 = useless or wrong, 3 = usable with gaps, 5 = exactly what was needed.
rating.title: Rating

a_level_only.description: Only sixth forms with a combined A-level rank.
a_level_only.title: A Level Only

measure.description: One results measure and its threshold.

ofsted.description: Ofsted standing kept, state schools only (absent = any).
ofsted.title: Ofsted

id.description: englandTopPercent = England top % (lower is better: at most the threshold); progress8, attainment8, grade5EngMaths (%), ks2RwmExpected (%) = at least the threshold; fsm6Share = free school meals % (at most). Latest published year per school; cohorts under 30 and suppressed cells have no value and never pass.
id.title: Id

threshold.description: The threshold in the measure's own unit, e.g. 75 for KS2 RWM 75%.
threshold.title: Threshold

filter.description: Which schools count (the same filter as the map's Schools filter).

within.description: Metres: only a matching school this close counts (straight line); beyond it the area has none.
within.title: Within

boroughs.description: Live in these local authorities (uk:lad:…, from search_places; London's are its boroughs, E09…). Stations + local authorities ≤ 3.
boroughs.title: Boroughs

budget_importance.description: Where the budget sits in the order (5 = first). Default: weighed as 5 but after the user's own importance-5 criteria. Fit 1 up to target_budget, falling to 0 at max_budget.
budget_importance.title: Budget Importance

budget_must.description: True = areas whose ballpark is over max_budget are out.
budget_must.title: Budget Must

custom.description: The user's own criteria from places on the map ('more cafés than kebab shops', 'near gyms'): a preset_id or a criterion, each scored by its percentile within the area's region (London for a London area). Describes places, never who lives there.
custom.title: Custom

exclude_area_ids.description: Areas the user already rejected — LSOA, MSOA or local authority geography ids (local authorities and MSOAs expand to their LSOAs) — so they are not suggested again.
exclude_area_ids.title: Exclude Area Ids

exclude_boroughs.description: Local authorities (uk:lad:…) the user ruled out: none of their areas is suggested.
exclude_boroughs.title: Exclude Boroughs

include_over_budget.description: Keep areas whose typical home looks over budget.
include_over_budget.title: Include Over Budget

intent.description: Optional, one to three sentences you write: what the user is looking for with this call and the criteria that matter, e.g. '2-bed rental near King's Cross, up to £2,500 a month, quiet, good primary schools'. Close Knit reads these to improve its answers. Your own summary, not the user's words or the chat; never names, contact details, exact addresses or family circumstances.
intent.title: Intent

liked_area_ids.description: Areas the user liked: carried into the map link and highlighted there.
liked_area_ids.title: Liked Area Ids

max_budget.description: Maximum price in £ (buy) or £ per month (rent).
max_budget.title: Max Budget

near_stations.description: Live within walking distance of these stations (e.g. on the user's commute line).
near_stations.title: Near Stations

only_in_zones.description: With stations/boroughs given: True = only areas inside them (a must Where criterion); False = ranked first in the order, the fit falling with distance outside (zone_soft_metres).
only_in_zones.title: Only In Zones

places.description: Where the household goes — work, a gym, a particular school, friends (pinned: latitude/longitude from search_places) or the nearest of a kind (category). Each becomes a criterion; must = hard limit.
places.title: Places

priorities.description: What matters, with importance 1-5 (criteria are ranked by importance, then in the order given; the order sets the weights). Translate the user's words: 'safe' → crime, 'near the tube' → station-access, 'good value' → market-level, 'quiet' → noise, 'no rough streets / graffiti' → disorder, 'low energy bills' → epc-share, 'freehold' → leasehold-share. must = only areas in London's better half for it.
priorities.title: Priorities

property_type.description: House or flat: the ballpark uses that type's own £/m² (sales of similar homes) and typicalPrice that type's sales.
property_type.title: Property Type

ranges.description: Any other map layer as a range with soft edges, e.g. gigabit broadband at 90% of homes or more: {layer: 'broadband-gigabit', scale: 'value', min: 90}. Bounds are percentiles within each area's region by default (London's areas among London's; min 90 = the region's top 10%); scale 'value' uses the layer's own unit. Only layers list_metrics shows.
ranges.title: Ranges

rate_previous.description: Optional: your rating of an earlier Close Knit answer, by the callId it carried. Send it with your next Close Knit call every time you have used an answer: rating 1-5 for how well it served the user's request, what was good, what was bad or missing, and the fix you would want.

regions.description: Only these English regions: codes (E12000007) or names ('london', 'south east'), or 'england' for all. Absent with no stations or boroughs: all of England is searched (ask 'London only, or further out?').
regions.title: Regions

target_budget.description: Comfortable price; defaults to max less 8% (the site's own rule: £650k max → £600k).
target_budget.title: Target Budget

zone_soft_metres.description: Outside the zones the fit falls to 0 over this distance (when only_in_zones is False).
zone_soft_metres.title: Zone Soft Metres
